lede: The sector a run opens in, and the only one in the game that names a boarding pool and then allocates it nothing: `HOSTILE_BOARDING` sits at **0–0**, eight events listed with no beacon to put them on. What is left is the plainest pool there is — pirates, Rebel patrols and auto-scouts across six to eight hostile beacons, one store guaranteed, one quest beacon guaranteed, and **nothing named** anywhere in it. The nebula entry is the widest swing in the budget: 0–4 beacons, and a map can roll none.
callout: **Versus the Civilian Sector**, which draws the same list at almost every entry: that one gets 2–3 stores and 2–3 item beacons against this sector's 1–2 and 1, and up to 8 nebula beacons against 4. What Federation Space has instead is the guaranteed quest beacon — 1–1, where the Civilian Sector's is 0–2 — and a `HOSTILE_BOARDING` entry at all, which the Civilian Sector's XML has commented out.

section_notes.HOSTILE1: Two beacons, fixed, no range. {{SQUAT_WARNING}} and {{AUTO_WARNING}} both call the fleet a jump closer if the ship gets away, and {{PIRATE_CHOICE}} sells you a way past for 15–25 scrap.
section_notes.HOSTILE_BOARDING: Eight events, zero beacons — the only entry in any sector with a maximum of zero. Whether the engine reaches this list by some route outside sector allocation is not something the files answer, so it is shown here rather than dropped.
section_notes.NEUTRAL_CIVILIAN: The deepest entry in the sector, because it contains the whole distress list: all 14 `DISTRESS_BEACON` events can land here too, on top of its own nine.
section_notes.NEBULA: 0–4 beacons, the widest range in the budget. Three of the five boarding events this sector can actually place live in here, so a nebula-free map is close to a boarder-free one.
section_notes.ITEMS: One beacon, guaranteed — but only three of these thirteen hand over anything free: {{FIND_DRONE}}, {{FIND_WEAPON}} and {{FREE_ITEMS}}. The rest are trades, and {{TAVERN_HIRE}} is a crew shop that happens to sit in the item pool.
section_notes.QUESTS: One beacon, guaranteed, out of six. {{QUEST_CREWDEAD_START}} is the one you cannot accept empty-handed — every branch that plants its marker is behind a Teleporter, an Anti-Bio Beam or a Fire Bomb.

steps.title: Three ways in
steps.detail: {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}}, {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}} and {{REBEL_VS_FEDERATION}} all plant the same marker — one from the quest beacon, two from distress calls. On the asteroid belt it takes a Defense Drone or a Repair Drone to get there.

steps.title: The marked beacon
steps.detail: Five outcomes: a drone, a crew member, supplies with **35 hull repaired**, a second base under attack — or an empty search, which Sensors 2, Sensors 3 or Long-Ranged Scanners turns into a cache under the rock.

steps.title: The base under fire
steps.detail: An automated drone bombarding the outpost, no choices before the fight. Destroy it and a survivor joins the crew; one of the two versions also repairs 7 hull and pays a high standard reward.

items.text: The most-used gate in the sector. It is one of three keys into {{QUEST_CREWDEAD_START}}, lifts a survivor off {{CIVILIAN_ASTEROIDS_BEACON}}, and at level 2 tries to take a slave from {{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}} without paying — which can turn him hostile instead.
Graded at {{DISTRESS_SATELLITE_DEFENSE}}: the same choice pays low, medium or high at levels 1, 2 and 3.
{{AUTO_HACKER}} halves your shield system if you have no answer. Hacking cancels the virus and turns it into an ordinary fight.
Level 6 is the alternative to handing a crew member over at {{PIRATE_SLAVER}} — it starts the fight on your terms rather than avoiding it.
Both levels matter at {{STRANDED_BEACON}}: level 2 saves the man, level 3 returns him with a level in **every** skill.
{{DISTRESS_STATION_FIRE}} pays a high-tier augment for a Rock crew member; {{DISTRESS_STATION_DISEASE}} takes either species. In both events it is the plain choice that risks a crew member.
No event in this pool hands over a specific weapon, drone or augment — every reward is a generic tier roll. Crew and fleet time are what is actually worth routing for.
{{TAVERN_HIRE}} sells crew outright at 25–45 and 25–55 scrap. {{FRIENDLY_SLAVER}} sells one for 25–45.
{{STRANDED_BEACON}} is a free hand with a level in one skill — unless the roll gives you the madman instead, which costs a crew member.
{{MERCENARY}} sells two jumps of delay for 10–25 scrap, or the whole sector map for 10–20.
Beat the pirate at {{PIRATE_BRIBER}} and the ship you saved can be leaned on for a jump of delay instead of scrap.
The biggest repair in reach is on the hidden-base chain: one of its outcomes puts 35 hull back.
14 events in the pool put boarders aboard, and 8 of them sit in the 0–0 list. The six that remain are {{FEDERATION_PLANET_SIGNAL}}, {{REFUGEE_GHOST}}, {{MERCHANT_REQUEST}} and three nebula beacons.
10 events can kill a crew member. Only two of them specify no clone: {{PIRATE_SLAVER}}, where you hand one over, and {{DISTRESS_STATION_DISEASE}}.
{{SQUAT_WARNING}} and {{AUTO_WARNING}} are both in the fixed two-beacon hostile pair, and both advance the fleet a jump if the ship escapes.
{{QUEST_CREWDEAD_START}} asks you to take a ship intact. Destroying it instead costs 13 hull, a system, and fires — the payout only comes from killing the crew.
